📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a new deal, with injury problems not helping the defender’s case.

In a recent development, he told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

“His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these issues stack up eventually.

“It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a latest contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

“If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with upcoming players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective new deals.

Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

As Lewis Steele rightly said, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

If this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a upcoming £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.

I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular new 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.

Industry observers note that interestingly, the meeting came in a week when Jacobo Solis, the influential Public Investment Fund executive and club director who is rarely seen in the city, was also present. The Spaniard’s involvement is viewed as extremely significant by those close to the project, and we understand an announcement on the club’s stadium aims is now ‘very close’.

The high-level meeting with Goldman Sachs is a major indication the club's board will recommend the development of a new stadium rather than redeveloping St James’, and I understand the former is currently the preference.

There has been significant outlay on various surveys around Leazes Park in recent months. I reported in April how the presence of bats in the area was one environmental complication they had to overcome. The club has since undertaken extensive work around animal and plant life.

The alternative remains a St James’ expansion, taking the capacity to 60,000, but chief executive David Hopkinson and others among the top brass are well aware that only a new, multi-purpose home would allow Newcastle to compete financially with the world’s biggest clubs.

A secret meeting with representatives from Goldman Sachs is the strongest indication yet the club are preparing to leave St James' Park rather than redevelop it.

In a recent development, in April, Daily Mail Sport revealed an architect’s drawing of how the new, three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated.

Aims of the new stadium reveal an exterior that has been likened to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena.

The proposed funding model combines borrowing, owner investment and potentially outside investors, with the debt sitting with Newcastle rather than the ownership. That makes the involvement of Goldman Sachs particularly significant as the club look to turn their ambitious plans into a financially viable reality.

Sources have described the circular design of a fresh stadium, and in April we revealed an architect’s drawing of how the three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated, but the exterior has been likened to both Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium by those who have seen images and video.

It has been revealed that club sources say they are continuing to work on options and plans for a latest stadium. But the visit of Goldman Sachs – and the simultaneous presence of one of PIF's most influential figures – suggests that work behind the scenes is moving towards a decisive stage.

Having covered this story for several years, I now believe PIF will be asked to sign off on a new stadium development ahead of an announcement in early 2027.

Dedic case closed - but he's told to bow out.

Amar Dedic has been given a rap on the knuckles and handed over his bow and arrows after the Newcastle defender’s ‘suspicious activity’ triggered a major police operation earlier this month.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on November 5 that the Bosnian was at the centre of a search involving at least six patrol cars after he was spotted carrying the hunting weaponry at a Northumberland beauty spot.

A concerned 999 caller, believing there could be a threat to the public, reported seeing him and a friend walking with the equipment near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the Harlow Hill area, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were intercepted in a blaze of blue lights around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic and his friend. After lengthy discussions at the roadside, police were satisfied that Dedic was using the weaponry for recreational use, but their investigation remained open.

However, I can confirm the matter is now closed and the 24-year-old has been reminded of UK law by police and the club. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in this country.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson told me: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, November 4, we received a report of suspicious activity in the Harlow Hill area.

According to recent reports, ‘It was reported that two men had been witnessed in possession of bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road. Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

'At that time, it was understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Following a number of enquiries, this has now been confirmed. The two men have since forfeited the bow and arrows and words of advice have been given to the pair. The case has now been closed.’.

Dedic took the confusion in good spirit, posting a picture of Lord of the Rings character Legolas, known for his prowess with a bow and arrow, on his social media page.

Joelinton has not yet been ruled out of the Tyne-Wear derby, despite fears over a significant injury lay-off.

I revealed on November 4 that the Brazilian had suffered a fresh muscle strain and this was confirmed by Matthias Jaissle the following day. There has been a suggestion this week that the period out could extend towards Christmas, but sources have played down that possibility.

I understand Joelinton is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures. This could still be too soon for the visit of Sunderland on December 6, but the noises around the midfielder have definitely been more optimistic in the past 24 hours. The 30-year-old is expected to be the only senior absentee from the squad that takes on Arsenal this weekend.

Joelinton (left) is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures.

Newcastle will NOT be signing Gambian triallists Omar Marong and Alieu Saine. I understand that, while the 16-year-olds have impressed during a two-week stay, club chiefs have decided that those already on the books are of greater potential.

Marong and Saine played in a 6-0 win over the i2i International Soccer Academy on Friday, and winger Saine chipped in with two assists. However, while there is a feeling both will secure moves to Europe in due course, Newcastle will keep a watching brief for now.

Sources indicate that the pair are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and were identified by the club’s fresh global talent team. They caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals.

Sources indicate that neither player could have signed permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle were keen to assess their potential. It is likely that players of a similar profile from Africa will arrive on trial in the future.

Arteta to meet old foe at St James'.

According to recent reports, both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

Interestingly, the fourth official with whom Arteta clashed at Sunderland earlier this season will be on duty. Elliot Bell repeatedly warned Arteta not to step from his technical zone at the Stadium of Light.

Sources indicate that when the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban.

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel.

Industry observers note that in another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

It has been revealed that joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

Arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

Finally, after James Trafford starred during England's 3-2 win in Spain this week, a brilliant match I was lucky enough to cover, one reader reached out to ask about an XI of players Newcastle have missed out on.

The club tried to sign Trafford on three occasions under Eddie Howe, and even as recently as this summer he appeared destined for Tyneside.

So, with thanks to the idea from Ian Spencer, here is the ‘what might have been’ XI of Newcastle targets who came close to signing….

Newcastle's What Might Have Been XI (3-5-2): James Trafford; Abdukodir Khusanov, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marc Guehi; Ivan Fresneda, Johan Manzambi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, James Maddison, Victor Munoz; Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike.

Would this XI beat the current side? Answers in the comments below please!

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

Givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

Correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

Sparta Rotterdam 1-5 AZ Alkmaar.

Twente Enschede 2-1 Willem II Tilburg.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous l'attendiez, le voici, le voilà, le désormais fameux tour d'horizon des Verts partis s'exiler pour plus (et mieux) jouer.

In a recent development, tandis que leurs anciens coéquipiers ont frappé un grand coup en ramenant les 3pts de Reims, les joueurs prêtés par l’ASSE ont joué plus que d’ordinaire ce week-end, à défaut de briller particulièrement. Bonne nouvelle en effet, ils étaient 5 sur 9 alignés d’entrée en attendant le match du Rapid Bucarest ce soir.

Du côté des championnats étrangers, Igor Miladinovic confirme son statut de pilier au Partizan Belgrade. Il a ainsi vécu sa 12e titularisation en championnat ce week-end pour une nouvelle défaite sur la pelouse de l’MT Belgrade (1-2) dans un des nombreux derbies de la capitale serbe. Il totalise désormais 969 minutes de jeu (plus 113 en Coupe d’Europe) et le Partizan Belgrade reste 10e sur 14 après 16 journées.

Industry observers note that son voisin Strahinja Stojkovic a connu une troisième titularisation de suite (la 5e cette saison), pour une troisième défaite (0-2) avec l’OFK Belgrade désormais avant dernier du championnat. Stojkovic est donc relégable et compte désormais 386 minutes de jeu.

En Roumanie, avant le match du Rapid Bucarest ce soir, le temps de jeu de Annan restait réduit : 241 minutes en championnat, et une dernière titularisation (la 3e) qui remonte au 18 septembre.

Recent findings suggest that direction l’Espagne ou Lucas Stassin réalise un début de saison mitigé. Il était certes de nouveau titulaire avec le FC Séville dans le derby face au Betis et s’est montré actif, mais il n’a pas eu l’occasion de briller et est sorti à la vilaine 69e minute, avant que son équipe égalise (1-1). Il compte désormais 541 minutes de jeu en Liga en 8 matchs (6 titularisations et 2 sorties de banc) et a marqué 1 but et délivré 1 passe décisive.

En d2 espagnole, les choses se compliquent pour Aïmen Moueffek. Son équipe réagit … mais sans lui. Pour la 2e fois de suite, il est resté scotché sur le banc, et Cadix l’a emporté 3-0 sur la pelouse de l’équipe B de la Real Sociedad. Son bilan reste de 202 minutes de jeu en championnat (3 titularisations) et 45 en coupe, alors qu’ont déjà été jouées 15 journées de championnat.

Dans l’Hexagone, l’éclaircie bourguignonne se confirme : En effet, si Djylian N’Guessan a de nouveau vu son équipe s’imposer depuis le banc de touche et continue d’afficher un très maigre temps de jeu avec Brest (28 minutes de jeu depuis le début de saison), Pierre Ekwah a connu sa seconde titularisation de suite, avec un nul (1-1) décroché par Auxerre à Monaco. Il totalise désormais 223 minutes de jeu.

It has been revealed that A Pau toujours rien de neuf pour Luan Gadegbeku (photo) qui, après sa titularisation en Coupe, est retourné sur le banc ce week-end. Il reste sur son maigre total de 147 minutes de jeu (plus 90 en Coupe). En revanche Axel Dodote a connu une 7e titularisation sur la pelouse du Red Star avec Pau, la première depuis début septembre, profitant notamment de l’absence de Briançon en défense centrale. Hélas il est sorti à la 53e . Son temps de jeu est désormais de 526 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the upcoming Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for newly introduced Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of upcoming arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their latest season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

Sources indicate that the scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Sources indicate that alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

It has been revealed that more defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

Sources indicate that that goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

It has been revealed that newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Sources indicate that thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the fresh season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a substantial challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle stated.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

It has been revealed that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about fresh signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

Sources indicate that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle remarked he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he noted.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

It has been revealed that van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which shows his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their newly introduced deals.

Alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

It was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

According to recent reports, well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

According to recent reports, slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

Industry observers note that he is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

It has been revealed that the Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Recent findings suggest that regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

Confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

In the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

Since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Substantial Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a upcoming-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Liverpool need to see more from their big-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

  • According to recent reports, oswald Tanchot commente la magnifique dynamique de son équipe dans L’Est Républicain.

According to recent reports, après 13 journées, l’ASNL a déjà empoché plus de points (28) que sur l’ensemble du championnat de L2 de la saison 2021-2022 ponctuée par sa relégation en National (27 points) ! Restant sur une impressionnante série de 7 victoires avant de défier les leaders stéphanois le 5 décembre dans le Chaudron pour le match au sommet de la 14e journée, les surprenants dauphins nancéiens viennent d’égaler la plus grande série de succès de l’histoire du club au chardon. Cela faisait 52 ans que Nancy n’avait pas réussi une telle performance. Lors de cet exercice 1974-1975, un certain Michel Platini (19 ans à l’époque) avait réussi sa première saison pleine en claquant 17 pions en 32 matches de D2. Il s’était aussi illustré cette saison-là en marquant pas moins de 13 buts en Coupe de France dont 3 en 8e de finale contre son futur club stéphanois, qui filait alors vers son dernier doublé de l’histoire.

According to recent reports, oswald Tanchot commente la magnifique dynamique de son équipe dans L’Est Républicain. "Notre force, c’est d’avoir un vestiaire aussi sain. On a des joueurs qui sont dans une logique de collectif en permanence, ça se voit sur le terrain et ça nous aide à aller chercher les victoires. Les joueurs qui entrent dans l’équipe, que ce soit au coup d’envoi ou en cours de match, apportent souvent quelque chose. Il faut absolument garder cet état d’esprit. Il y a beaucoup de solidarité dans notre jeu, des fermetures de passes pour l’adversaire parce que tous nos joueurs font les efforts dans le replacement. Ces petits détails font une grande différence. On voulait se donner le droit d’avoir une affiche magnifique à Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais avant de penser à Saint-Etienne, on souhaite négocier au mieux ce 8e tour de Coupe de France contre Furiani (National 1).".

Gli altri avrebbero tirato di piattone, io sinceramente già lo stavo mandando a quel paese. Nel mio modo di pensare il calcio, quella giocata non m'è passata neanche per l'anticamera del cervello. Dico Rui Costa, dai.

Frattesi? Io non ho salvato la vita a nessuno. Lui è un capoccione, esagera sempre. Ha bisogno d'affetto, come tanti giocatori. Ha bisogno anche di prendere le mazzate nei denti, vuol giocare come dice lui. Il merito su quel che sta facendo è suo. Sono contento che abbia fatto gol di sinistro. Adesso recuperiamo due giorni e poi da martedì iniziano a preparare la sfida contro il Torino.

Qual è il segreto di questa Lazio? Noi proponiamo, però chi propone deve avere dall'altra parte gente che ci crede fortemente. Quando il giocatore la pensa in maniera diversa, lì viene il difficile. Bisogna esser bravi a fargli capire perché vogliamo fare determinate cose. Siamo stati bravi noi, sono bravi loro quando facciamo i lavori individuali. Con tutta questa organizzazione che abbiamo messo giù, loro si trovano bene. Noi proponiamo e per il momento tutto sta andando bene. La base di tutto è il lavoro: se vuoi giocare in questo modo qui, la fatica ti deve rimanere nella testa. A parlare è facile, non basta.

Industry observers note that L'ancien Vert, Vagner Dias Goncalves (32 ans) joue désormais, depuis le 1er septembre, en deuxième division chypriote, dans le club du FC Ethnikos Achnas. C'était, ce week-end la 8ème journée du championnat, et les  coéquipiers de Vagner l'ont largement emporté (7-0) sur ASIL Lysi. Titulaire pour la 1ère fois de la saison, l'ancien Vert a inscrit un doublé aux 2ème et 31ème minutes. Le FC Ethnikos Achnas est leader avec 7 victoires et 1 défaite.

Les images du match, c'est ici.

In a recent development, le Capverdien Vagner Dias Goncalves était arrivé à l'ASSE en 2017. La saison 2017-2018, il avait participé à 4 matchs de L1 (106 minutes de jeu), et un match de Coupe de France. Le plus souvent en équipe N3 de Laurent Batlles, il avait accédé à la N2 et inscrit 6 buts.La saison suivante, 2018-2019, il n'a fait aucune apparition en pro, jouant donc en N2, toujours sous les ordres de Laurent Batlles. Il y inscrit 6 buts mais ne convainc pas au point d'être prêté à l'AS Nancy (en 2 saisons, il joue 33 matchs et inscrit 13 buts) puis transféré au FC Metz en 2020. Le club lorrain le prêtera au FC Sion (2021-2022) puis au RFC Seraing, en Belgique, (2022-2023) où il avait retrouvé Aurélien Remoué et Marvin Tshibuabua.

En janvier 2024, il a signé dans le club polonais de de Radomiak Radom, puis en mai 2025 dans le club brésilien d'Amazonas pour une pige de 4 mois. Sans club pendant un an, il a rejoint, le mois dernier, le championnat de Chypre.

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its fresh ambassador.

Now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’.

BC.GAME, an online casino company, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Leicester City have axed a partnership with BC.GAME, after the gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador.

Leicester confirmed fans who have purchased a replica shirt featuring the sponsor's name within the last 28 days can return it for a full refund or exchange by December 2.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too.

In recent years, Leicester’s spectacular decline on the pitch has mirrored the relationship with their supporters.

During the years immediately before and after their stunning Premier League triumph in 2016, it was difficult to find a club more in tune with the fanbase.

But a series of baffling decisions – including the tie-up with BC.GAME – eroded trust between the club and their supporters.

Leicester are now in League One and face a long road back but sensible moves like this one suggest they are at least facing in the right direction again.

Morgan Guilavogui (28 ans), le jeune frère de Josuha évolue en MLS (Conférence ouest), au Real Salt Lake, depuis le 3 février 2026, après avoir porté les couleurs de l'ASSE (formation), du SC Toulon, du Paris FC, du RC Lens et du FC St Pauli.

Vendredi, à l'heure de jeu, contre les Seattle Sounders, dans les playoffs de la MLS Cup, il a inscrit le but égalisateur d'un superbe tir de la demi-lune, tir qui s'est logé dans la lucarne adverse . Le match s'est terminé sur un nul (1-1) mais les coéquipiers de Morgan Guilavogui l'ont emporté 3-5 aux tirs au but. L'autre ancien Vert, Alexandros Katranis n'était pas sur la feuille de match. C'était le 5ème but de la saison pour Morgan Guilavogui. (1 en Leagues Cup, 5 en MLS League soccre, et 1 en MLS Cup Playoffs).

Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
  • Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
  • According to recent reports, signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

According to recent reports, signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

In a recent development, emery mentioned: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they demonstrated they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

According to recent reports, this was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another crucial player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

In a recent development, the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Industry observers note that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

According to recent reports, it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Recent findings suggest that before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a major chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

In a recent development, PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

In a recent development, it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

According to recent reports, after the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the newly introduced Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

There will be five added minutes.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

Industry observers note that the ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

According to recent reports, PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Sources indicate that aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

Industry observers note that the space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

According to recent reports, the VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

Recent findings suggest that doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Sources indicate that cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

In a recent development, mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

In a recent development, other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

We are back under way in Salzburg.

Brian Madjo - remember the name.

In a recent development, incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

According to recent reports, the teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17.

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

Sources indicate that on the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth major chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes concerns for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Sources indicate that madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

In a recent development, referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly upcoming rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

Sources indicate that PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia highlights great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

Sources indicate that as you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

According to recent reports, tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

According to recent reports, this is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

It has been revealed that mcGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

According to recent reports, some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:.

PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo.

Industry observers note that lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

In a recent development, PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

It has been revealed that “There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”.

These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. Recent findings suggest that “I feel like the club is in a latest era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

According to recent reports, PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

Sources indicate that “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

In a recent development, “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

In a recent development, il y a des déplacements champêtres en Coupe de France qui ressemblent à des pièges (les Verts en savent quelque chose) mais celui des Amazones hier après-midi à Guéret à l'occasion du 1er tour fédéral, a plutôt ressemblé à une aimable promenade bucolique.Face aux féminines de l'ES Guérétoise (Régionale 2), les protégées de Yannick Chandioux ont transformé leur entrée en lice dans la compétition en véritable feu d'artifice avec un cinglant 13-0.Leader de Seconde Ligue, le coach stéphanois avait logiquement décidé de s'appuyer sur un onze largement remanié, tout en conservant suffisamment de cadres, tel qu'Ithaisa Viñoly, étonnamment préférée à Emma Templier, ainsi que Mathilde Kack ou Lorna Chicha Douvier. La surprise du chef avait pour nom Jalia Chabourine, 20 ans, pour sa première titularisation en verte. Et le moins que l'on puisse dire, c'est que la jeune Francilienne n'aura pas traîné pour trouver la bonne carburation: dès la 7e minute, elle ouvrait le bal d'une tête bien placée, à la réception d'un service de Jana Zufankova (0-1) suivie par Héloïse Mansuy, capitaine d'un jour, à la 15e minute (0-2). Le temps que Dona Scannapieco loupe un penalty et le vrai festival commençait avec d'abord Lorna Chicha Douvier (0-3) puis un triplé de Jalia Chabourine en 5 minutes (23e, 25e, 28e). Un quadruplé express qui la plaçait en tête des buteuses de la saison avec Mansuy et Isgrig (5 buts). Dona Scannapieco ajoutait une 7e pierre à l'édifice à la 37e minute avant que Chabourine ne signe son cinquième but personnel à la 41e, faisant d'elle la meilleure réalisatrice de la saison ! Roxane Couasnon concluait cette première période totalement à sens unique à la 43e minute (0-9) avant que la mi-temps ne préserve les Guérétoises pendant un petit quart d'heure...Au retour des vestiaires, les Stéphanoises levaient légèrement le pied et ne marquaient plus que 4 buts par l'intermédiaire de Scannapieco (70e et 84e), Belhout-Achi (81e) et Chicha Douvier (89e) encore.On aura également noté l'apparition de la jeune Thaïs Aznar pour son troisième match pro, un an après le dernier en Coupe LFFP.

Au-delà de la qualification, cette victoire restera dans les annales de la section féminine stéphanoise. Avec treize buts inscrits, les Amazones signent le plus large succès officiel recensé de l'histoire de l'équipe. Yannick Chandioux: "Je suis satisfait de l’image que l’équipe a donnée. On a fait une bonne entame, ce qui nous a permis de marquer rapidement. C’est intéressant dans ce type de matchs (...) Je souhaite également féliciter Jalia Chabourine, qui a eu moins de temps de jeu depuis le début de saison et qui a réussi aujourd’hui à inscrire cinq buts (...) Notre objectif principal est de remonter en Arkema Première Ligue, mais si l’on peut faire un joli parcours en Coupe de France, c’est toujours bon à prendre. Si on a marqué l’histoire, c’est top. Ce n’est pas ce qui m’intéresse le plus aujourd’hui, mais c’est toujours sympathique de contribuer à établir de nouveaux records pour la section féminine.L'aventure en Coupe de France se poursuivra au deuxième tour fédéral face à Montauban (D3), qui a obtenu sa qualification en dominant Bayonne (7-1).

Quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde, Teddy Riner a bâti un palmarès exceptionnel qui le place au sommet de sa discipline. Alors que son avenir sportif restait au cœur des discussions depuis les Jeux de Paris, le Français surprend en ouvrant un tout autre chapitre personnel. Un virage spectaculaire.

Dans une vidéo publiée ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 sur son compte X, Teddy Riner a pris la parole face caméra afin de lever le voile sur ses intentions pour la prochaine présidentielle. Le judoka de 37 ans a officialisé sa démarche avec des mots simples et directs.

Conscient des réactions que son entrée en politique peut susciter, le quintuple champion olympique a tenu à devancer immédiatement les critiques concernant son manque d'expérience dans les fonctions publiques. Teddy Riner a ainsi déclaré : « Je sais ce qu'on va dire de moi. Il est fou, il n'est pas du sérail, il n'a pas les codes, il n'a jamais fait de politique. Mais posez-vous la question avec moi, qu'est-ce qui est fou aujourd'hui ? Je n'ai pas passé ma vie derrière un public, mais le combat a toujours fait partie de moi. » Une détermination affichée.

Recent findings suggest that pour concrétiser ses ambitions, le judoka français de 37 ans a également fondé sa propre formation politique ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, baptisée « La France qu'on veut ». Cette prise de parole sur les réseaux sociaux a d'ailleurs été accompagnée d'un entretien accordé au quotidien Le Parisien pour préciser le sens de sa démarche. Dans cet échange, Teddy Riner revendique une volonté de rassemblement sans affiliation partisane, affirmant vouloir devenir un « président qui fédère » sans se situer à droite ou à gauche.

Ainsi, son mouvement politique refuse d'entrer dans les clivages traditionnels pour privilégier une adhésion commune à l'échelle du pays. Un projet ambitieux.

Recent findings suggest that toutefois, cette ambition politique ne pousse pas Teddy Riner vers la retraite sportive. Sur le initiative des compétitions, sa dernière apparition individuelle remonte aux Jeux olympiques de Paris en août 2024, suivie d'une participation sous les couleurs du PSG Judo en Ligue des champions en décembre 2024. Malgré cette nouvelle démarche politique, le quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde de judo demeure bel et bien un athlète en activité.

According to recent reports, au-delà de l'élection présidentielle de 2027, Teddy Riner a ainsi fait part de son souhait de participer aux Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028 si ses futures responsabilités et les Français le lui permettent. Le judoka français lie donc son avenir sportif à la suite de son engagement public, avec en ligne de mire les Jeux olympiques de Los Angeles 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Auteur de son premier but dans l'élite lors du match nul sur le terrain sarthois, Mamadou Coulibaly a suscité une vive polémique en mimant un geste d'égorgement. Le jeune milieu de l'AS Monaco se retrouve désormais sous la menace directe d'une lourde suspension.

Recent findings suggest that dimanche 8 novembre 2026, l'AS Monaco a été accrochée sur la pelouse du Mans FC (1-1) pour le compte de la 10e journée de Ligue 1. Si le club du Rocher espérait engranger des points précieux, la rencontre a été marquée par le geste de son joueur de 22 ans.

Titularisé dans l'entrejeu monégasque, Mamadou Coulibaly pensait passer une bonne soirée après avoir ouvert le score à la 40e minute de jeu. Mais la joie d'inscrire son tout premier but en Ligue 1 a rapidement viré au malaise lors de sa célébration. Le milieu monégasque s'est en effet dirigé vers le poteau de corner pour glisser sur les genoux, avant de tirer la langue et de mimer un geste d'égorgement avec son pouce sous la gorge. Un geste polémique.

Sources indicate that ce geste n'est malheureusement pas inédit en Principauté cette saison. En effet, cette célébration reproduit à l'identique celle effectuée par son partenaire de club Paris Brunner face à Strasbourg en septembre dernier, lors de la 4e journée de Ligue 1. Pour ce geste, le jeune attaquant avait été sanctionné par la commission de discipline de la LFP de quatre matches de suspension, dont deux fermes et deux avec sursis.

D'ailleurs, cette récidive au sein du même effectif met le joueur dans une situation extrêmement délicate. En raison de ce précédent disciplinaire très récent, Mamadou Coulibaly risque une sanction similaire d'au moins deux matches de suspension ferme devant la commission de discipline de la LFP. L'instance disciplinaire devrait se saisir rapidement du dossier pour trancher sur ce comportement. Un coup dur en perspective.

According to recent reports, conscient des remous provoqués par son geste, le joueur de 22 ans s'est exprimé devant les journalistes à l'issue de la rencontre. « Je tiens à m’excuser parce que j’ai cru comprendre que ça avait été mal compris. C’est un geste que j’ai fait par rapport un ami à moi qui m’a conseillé au sujet de la célébration. Je tiens à m'excuser si ça a pu heurter des gens. Maintenant, ce sont des choses qui se font dans d'autres championnats, je n'ai pas pensé que ça pourrait avoir des conséquences négatives », a ainsi déclaré Mamadou Coulibaly en zone mixte au micro des médias après Le Mans-Monaco.

Toutefois, cette justification risque de ne pas suffire auprès de son entraîneur Filipe Luis. Le coach monégasque avait pourtant publiquement averti son groupe en septembre après l'affaire similaire, insistant sur l'exemplarité attendue : « Il a fait une erreur. Il l'a compris tout de suite. Il s'est excusé. Le club prend cette affaire très au sérieux (…). On espère que ça ne se reproduira plus », avait prévenu le technicien en conférence de presse. Au-delà de cette polémique extra-sportive, l'AS Monaco accueillera l'AJ Auxerre au stade Louis-II le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 20h45 pour la 11e journée de Ligue 1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.

The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.

His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

He told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He indicates he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”.

The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

We can understand Szoboszlai wanting to represent his country, especially in his role as captain, but those who pay his wages at Anfield mightn’t have been overly impressed with his decision to play on despite knowing prior to the Georgia match that he wasn’t operating at 100%.

That Liverpool don’t play until Sunday at 4:30pm gives the 26-year-old that bit of additional time to manage his fitness carefully so that he’s in prime condition for the game against Manchester United.

Industry observers note that whether or not the midfielder will start that match is debatable. The in-form Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz will likely have two of the three midfield berths nailed down, and the excellent displays of Trey Nyoni have made it difficult to omit him from the XI.

Also, if Iraola feels that Szoboszlai isn’t fully fit by Sunday, he probably won’t take the risk of throwing our number 8 back into the starting line-up, instead keeping him in reserve should he be needed off the bench.

Hopefully the influential Hungarian won’t suffer any further complications over the next four days, and everyone associated with Liverpool will surely be glad that the international window is out of the way, with the next one not upon us until late March 2027.
