📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026.

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

In a recent development, news of newly introduced contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s newly introduced contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on latest contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year.

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree new terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month.

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

According to recent reports, he told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

It has been revealed that ‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’.

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

Now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The initiative to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

In a recent development, the biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

The injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next major decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain important to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

It has been revealed that mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed upcoming long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Substantial Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

It has been revealed that the environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be said for stars at every club in the league.

According to recent reports, there’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his newly introduced midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager said: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’.

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement.

Sources indicate that the collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal.

In a recent development, this season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Recent findings suggest that berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 08:14 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 10:33 EST, 19 November 2026.

Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s new head coach.

United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.

They show that United brought in total revenues of £146.1m compared to £140.3m in the first quarter last year, but made an operating loss for the quarter of £3m compared with an operating profit of £13m 12 months ago.

The results come just weeks after co-owner Avram Glazer told a conference that the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

Sources say that United acted early in the season to address the drop in form under Carrick that saw United slide into the relegation zone, and the club are now focused on improving results under Pochettino.

The Argentine is expected to be given a modest transfer budget in January to make newly introduced signings, with United in the market for a striker, left-back and centre-back.

Man United's latest financial results come after the Glazers mentioned that success isn't dependent on results.

The results don't include the £10m United paid to buy Pochettino and his staff from the US national team.

In a recent development, chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘Our revenue remains strong and on track, while we continue to grow sustainably. We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch.’.

The latest results only cover the first five Premier League fixtures of the season, one Champions League match and the League Cup defeat to Brighton. Sources insist that they show the benefit of the cost-cutting under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos and what they say is improved operational efficiency.

United have reiterated their guidance of total revenues of £740-£760m for this financial year after reporting that the first quarter saw rises in broadcast (£5.3m), retail (£1.3m) and matchday (£0.6m) revenues.

However, sponsorship revenue was down by £1.4m despite a new training kit deal with Betway, largely due to United playing individual pre-season friendlies rather than going on summer tour.

Employee benefit expenses for the quarter were £79.9m, an increase of £6.3m due mainly to players' wages going up 25 per cent after qualifying for the Champions League.

United's borrowing has increased 19 per cent from a year ago, with the club's historic US dollar debt up $125m to $775m 'as a result of the refinancing of our senior secured notes in June 2026'.

This rise, which was revealed in the last set of results in September, equates to £577.4m, up from £481.2m. The net cost of financing that debt dropped from £21.4m to £14.5m.

Meanwhile, United’s borrowing on the club's revolving credit facility was £207.1m as of September 30, down from £268m a year ago.

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic upcoming look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his upcoming buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

In a recent development, pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's latest haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

In a recent development, so far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many notable things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

Sources indicate that maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jonathan Tah has stated he would like to see Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz at Bayern Munich.

The duo, of course, have history having played together at Bayer Leverkusen, where they did the domestic double in 2023/24, lifting the Bundesliga and DFB Pokal titles.

Sources indicate that speaking at a fan club meeting, Tah was asked which player he would love to have at Bayern, stating: “Flo Wirtz. First of all, he’s a good friend of mine. I know what qualities he has on the pitch and what he can bring to a team. That’s why it would definitely be him.”.

Industry observers note that in the summer of 2025, Bayern Munich were close to securing a deal for Wirtz before the German attacking midfielder chose Anfield. After a £116m move to Liverpool, Wirtz struggled to make an impact in his first season.

However, the 23-year-old seems to have found his feet under Andoni Iraola. On Sunday, he was voted Man of the Match after his goal and assist helps Liverpool put four past Manchester United in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

Wirtz is showing his best qualities for the German national team as well. During the last international break, he scored a goal against Serbia and two against the Netherlands.

Speaking on whether Wirtz has ‘returned from international duty with more confidence’, Iraola said: “ No, I think he has been playing very well for a long, sustained period of time. He finished before the break with a goal and an assist against Crystal Palace, an assist the game before. He has consistently been playing well for a good period of time. He’s going to maybe continue playing well sometimes without an assist, without a goal, but still, I think he is giving us a lot.”.

While there are no concrete offers for Wirtz at the moment, it was reported back in September that Bayern remain open to signing the Liverpool man if an opportunity presents itself.

Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
  • Sources indicate that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
  • Sources indicate that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

Sources indicate that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

Sources indicate that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

According to recent reports, A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

It has been revealed that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca stated, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

According to recent reports, momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

In a recent development, marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

Sources indicate that marco Rose, their upcoming manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he stated. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

According to recent reports, they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his fresh manager.

Sources indicate that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

It has been revealed that city will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a major ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “upcoming Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca noted “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

In a recent development, of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a latest season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

In a recent development, the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Industry observers note that emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Recent findings suggest that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

Recent findings suggest that guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Sources indicate that bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

It has been revealed that foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

According to recent reports, ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Sources indicate that bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Industry observers note that chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

According to recent reports, villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

In a recent development, city are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Demonstrates how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

In a recent development, brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

It has been revealed that de Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Sources indicate that play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

We’re back under way at the Amex.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

In a recent development, pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

According to recent reports, ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

In a recent development, moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

Sources indicate that VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he mentioned of Guardiola’s grand design.

Recent findings suggest that tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s substantial idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

According to recent reports, describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

According to recent reports, the Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

It has been revealed that brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “I will be speaking with Bayern in the near future about what happens next, what the club wants,” he exclusively told Kicker.
  • Sources indicate that ulreich had been number two behind Manuel Neuer for several years at Bayern before dropping behind Jonas Urbig in the pecking order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich goalkeeper Sven Ulreich stated that he is yet to make a decision about his future.

“I will be speaking with Bayern in the near future about what happens next, what the club wants,” he exclusively told Kicker.

Sources indicate that ulreich had been number two behind Manuel Neuer for several years at Bayern before dropping behind Jonas Urbig in the pecking order. With the likely situation that the World Cup-winning keeper can retire at the end of the season, Ulreich calling it a day on his career is also a possibility. “I can’t speak for Manu about what happens after the season, but it’s not like I’m making everything dependent on him,” he added.

Sitting on an expiring contract, the 38-year-old is open to anything that might happen going forward and understands things can change rapidly. “Anything is possible as long as I feel good, healthy, and fit. That’s the case at the moment. But I’ve also learned that things can change quickly. I live in the here and now, and right now I enjoy going out on the pitch every day,” he explained.

Bayern may struggle to find a reliable keeper like Ulreich, who admits that giving it your best in training and keeping the No.1 on their toes comes as part of the parcel. “It’s crucial to always try to deliver strong performances in training,” he remarked. “If only to show the goalkeeper in front of you, ‘hey, you have to give your all.’.

“He should also signal to the team that there’s someone back there who gives top performances in every training session.”.

While 23-year-old keeper Urbig is expected to be the long-term replacement for Neuer, Bayern are still looking for a good backup keeper – Finn Dahmen of Augsburg, Marvin Schwäbe of Cologne, and Loris Karius of Schalke, according to Bild’s ‘Bayern Insider’ podcast.

According to one report, Liverpool have the opportunity to snap up a full-back from a fellow European giant for a modest amount.

The Reds have found a solution to the problematic right-back position with the loan acquisition of Ronald Araujo, who was originally signed to add centre-back cover but has excelled on the flank at Anfield.

Despite the Barcelona loanee’s fine form, Jamie Carragher has implored his former club to move for a full-back in January if the right opportunity arises, and there might just be another one from Camp Nou.

As reported by Graeme Bailey for TEAMtalk, the LaLiga champions are prepared to sanction an exit for Alejandro Balde amid interest from Liverpool, with Barca head coach Hansi Flick indicating that the 23-year-old isn’t part of his prepares.

His representative Jorge Mendes has reportedly held talks with the Merseyside club to inform them of the conditions surrounding a potential deal for the player, who’s viewed by Anfield chiefs as an ‘attractive option’.

The agent is understood to have communicated a valuation of €40m (£33m) to prospective suitors, and that figure would apply whether the deal is structured as a permanent transfer or a loan arrangement with a purchase option.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Even though Balde has been overtaken by Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo in the left-back pecking order at Barcelona, Liverpool might still feel that the price point apparently quoted by Mendes would represent something of a bargain for the 23-year-old.

Catalan columnist Javier Miguel has previously hailed some ‘spectacular’ performances from the Spain international (AS), and an analysis from The Athletic highlighted his aptitude for taking on opposition full-backs whilst marauding along the left flank.

He’s also renowned for his pace, with his former agent Junior Minguella describing him as a ‘bullet’, and Flick previously spoke of how the Spain international strives to ‘get better every day’ (The Athletic).

If Kostas Tsimikas were to depart at the end of his contract next summer – certainly not an implausible scenario – then Liverpool would need to add left-back competition for Milos Kerkez, and Barcelona’s apparent readiness to offload Balde could play into our hands.

Considering the success we’ve had so far with Araujo, FSG might just be inclined to sound out the Catalan giants about potentially adding another full-back option from Flick’s squad in 2027. This could be an intriguing one to watch over the coming months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

In a recent development, it was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

Industry observers note that city owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

In a recent development, there are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also announced on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

Recent findings suggest that if an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Recent findings suggest that financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s issue had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

Quinn said that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that werder Bremen secured a memorable 4-0 victory over Hamburg in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. Marco Friedl, Justin Njinmah and Niclas Füllkrug all scored during an outstanding second-half performance at the Weserstadion, as Daniel Thioune’s side returned to winning ways following their defeat against Stuttgart.

Perhaps even more significant than the result was the manner in which Bremen dominated their northern rivals.

It has been revealed that after a goalless first half, Bremen broke the deadlock through captain Friedl in the 55th minute before Njinmah scored twice in four minutes to put the result beyond doubt. For Njinmah, who was making his first start since suffering an injury towards the end of August, his brace represented a particularly encouraging return.

Füllkrug completed the scoring in stoppage time, taking his Bundesliga tally to 10 goals in 10 matches since returning to Bremen.

Werder finished with 56% possession and seven shots on target compared to Hamburg’s one. Their attacking efficiency and defensive organisation made the difference.

The victory came just one day after Bremen announced that Thioune had agreed to extend his contract. There could hardly have been a better way to celebrate that announcement.

Bremen remain unbeaten at the Weserstadion this season, collecting 13 points from a possible 15 and winning nine of their last 10 Bundesliga home encounters against Hamburg.

For Merlin Polzin, the defeat highlighted Hamburg’s persistent problems away from home, having now lost five of their six away league matches this season.

In a recent development, bremen, meanwhile, continue to demonstrate how much progress they have made under Thioune. Their ability to remain patient, maintain defensive discipline and exploit opportunities in the second half reflects a team growing in confidence.

With 18 points from 10 matches, Werder have given their supporters genuine reasons for optimism. European qualification may still be a premature expectation, but performances like this suggest Bremen are gradually becoming a team capable of competing for considerably more than Bundesliga survival.

For now, however, northern Germany belongs to Werder Bremen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

It has been revealed that really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Sources indicate that dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

In a recent development, “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

In a recent development, one of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

According to recent reports, off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

In a recent development, this, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Industry observers note that cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

It has been revealed that but parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola noted. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

Why they didn’t follow the blueprint that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

In a recent development, “We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with fresh managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Latest Update: 'If you don't give him what he wants, he'll burn your house down': Inside the 'cult' of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as sources from his crumbling sporting empire reveal the destructive know-it-all arrogance of Man United co-owner and his henchmen

  • The ‘imprisonment’ of the four-time British Olympic champion in a building, with signs declaring ‘No Entry’ fixed to the external doors, was one of the more extraordinary allegations to emerge from the court case, settled this week, over a £180million yacht Ratcliffe and Ainslie built together for the 2024 America’s Cup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 12:11 EST, 19 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the flat rural acres of the Turweston Aerodrome, in the north-west corner of Buckinghamshire, are far enough from human habitation for anyone padlocked in a building out there to feel seriously threatened. And if the testimony of Sir Ben Ainslie is to be believed, that’s what can come of crossing swords with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The ‘imprisonment’ of the four-time British Olympic champion in a building, with signs declaring ‘No Entry’ fixed to the external doors, was one of the more extraordinary allegations to emerge from the court case, settled this week, over a £180million yacht Ratcliffe and Ainslie built together for the 2024 America’s Cup.

Sources indicate that ratcliffe, who had withdrawn financial support, was demanding the team’s assets and intellectual property, and, according to court papers, Ineos representative Raymond Fellows, assisted by two security contractors, arrived at the offices of Ainslie's Athena Racing and applied his own chain and padlock. He’d been refused the keys by the building’s owner. Ainslie and his financial officer Matt Robinson managed to leave the building through the fire escape.

Ineos were applying petrochemicals business methods to sport, as usual. Fellows had also been employed by Ratcliffe to provide security assistance amid protests at Ineos’ controversial British fracking sites. The experienced security industry executive observed that ‘a small hard core group of activists’ was at work and that social media surveillance was useful, according to court papers from an earlier case.

Ineos denied the ‘false imprisonment’ of Ainslie, insisting that their employee had padlocked the building to prevent anyone entering, not knowing that someone was inside and that, in any case, there were ‘alternative exit routes’.

Recent findings suggest that but the manufacturer did not entirely challenge Ainslie’s claim that Rob Nevin, chairman of Ratcliffe’s sports division and a Manchester United board member, had told him during a heated meeting about the disputed boat in Barcelona: ‘We have a phrase at Ineos: scorched earth. It means that if you don’t give Jim what he wants, he will burn your house down, or words to that effect.’.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe's relationship with his one-time friend Ben Ainslie ruptured after Ineos withdrew support for the latter's America’s Cup bid.

In a recent development, ratcliffe's running of Manchester United is criticised by one anonymous source. ‘People like him see football on TV and just assume they can do it,’ they say.

That threat, which Ineos say was only made figuratively, illustrates how Ratcliffe runs his businesses with what several sources describe as a cult-like authority, full of such maxims and mantras laid down to staff who fear him.

That ‘cult of Sir Jim’ is born of the billionaire’s own immense air of superiority and is something he seems to have instilled in some of his most senior executives.

According to recent reports, nevin, 68, a long-standing Ratcliffe lieutenant, has informed some who have encountered him since he arrived at Old Trafford that he has completed 60 or more major ‘transactions’ – business deals – in the oil and gas industry. He is described as ‘not short on confidence’.

Sources indicate that nevin chairs Ineos Sport, the collection of acquisitions built up when Ratcliffe believed his firm could straddle multiple sports and succeed at all of them, in the style of Red Bull. Ratcliffe disastrously installed his brother, Bob, as chief executive at OGC Nice, the second of the football teams he bought, and that air of superiority and ‘always knowing’ has been manifest at United, too.

Ratcliffe demonstrated to some of the Manchester United players the stretches he was using for London Marathon training, after buying the club. He considered his friend Sir Dave Brailsford to be ‘best in class’ when it came to running the football side of the club, despite the former Team Sky cycling chief only having a loose connection of football contacts, mostly picked up from his appearances on the Leaders in Sport conference circuit for his friend Jimmy Worrall, the entrepreneur who set up that business.

Sources have told us that Brailsford was so enamoured with Manchester City, after arriving to ‘save United’, that he and other Ineos people were ‘skipping around’ when Omar Berrada, chief operations officer at the Etihad, was hired as chief executive.

In a recent development, ‘There was no sense from Ratcliffe of needing people who understand the industry and its craft,’ says one source, speaking on condition of anonymity. ‘People like this see football on TV and just assume they can do it.’.

Ratcliffe (pictured next to former United boss Erik ten Hag) inexplicably considered Dave Brailsford (right) to be ‘best in class’ when it came to running the football side of the club.

Rob Nevin (right) chairs Ineos Sport, the collection of acquisitions built up when Ratcliffe wrongly believed his firm could straddle multiple sports and succeed at all of them.

In a recent development, none of Ratcliffe’s executives will be wanting to tell him that. A further sense of what a formidable presence he is for his own staff came in a 30-minute ‘Ask Jim’ interview with him, conducted by his own director of corporate affairs, Tom Crotty, this summer.

Ratcliffe stares at the floor for much of the time as Crotty bowls him a series of long-hop questions and he seems profoundly miserable, revealing little more than his unhappiness with the British government’s management of North Sea oilfields and his dislike for the British sports press.

Sources indicate that the interview was conducted the day after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in July, which Ratcliffe attended. ‘It was fabulous. A great celebration, despite the whining British press who really didn’t like it,’ he says.

Asked how he switches off, he cites time on the golf driving range and fishing on his salmon farm in Iceland – to which Berrada and the Glazers have had to make their way for some executive meetings. ‘Biggest lessons learned in 2025?’ There don’t appear to have been any. At no stage do United feature.

Ratcliffe trots out his extremely well-worn mantra about the major three traits Ineos prize most – ‘Grit, rigour, humour’ – informing the relentlessly positive Crotty of the need to ‘do work properly before you make important decisions, because you need to spend capital well.’.

That’s not happened in sport. The extraordinary rupture with Ainslie, after Ineos withdrew support for a third America’s Cup cycle and he continued to use the boat, is part of a general, hugely acrimonious winding down of the Ineos Sport masterplan.

Sources indicate that OGC Nice and FC Lausanne-Sport, Ratcliffe’s European football clubs, are up for sale amid fan protest, while it is widely expected that Ineos will eventually disappear from cycling. They have already diluted their involvement, with the team formerly known as the Ineos Grenadiers now co-sponsored by Danish technology firm Netcompany. The All Blacks and Tottenham Hotspur both sued Ineos for prematurely terminating commercial relationships. Both parties ultimately reached a confidential legal settlement with the manufacturer.

What United need, as they look to Mauricio Pochettino for deliverance, is for Ratcliffe to climb down from his lofty peak, display some of the humility which has been missing and admit there have been faults.

What United need, as they look to Mauricio Pochettino for deliverance, is for Ratcliffe to display some humility.

The club's executives, including CEO Omar Berrada (centre) and director of football Jason Wilcox (right), have appeared out of their depth and in need of support.

Sources indicate that the view among some outsiders who interact at a high level with the club is, in the words of one, that United are ‘the biggest club in the world and yet no longer the biggest club in the world'. They carry huge expectation, yet are unable to compete for transfer fees and wages with Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City, and have removed excellent staff without replacing them. To cite only one, Victoria Timpson secured the club’s lucrative Snapdragon sponsorship deal but still departed.

In a recent development, ‘If United were an iPhone, someone would need to unfold the paper clip pretty quick, push it in the side of the phone and hard restart everything,’ says the aforementioned source. 'The club need a genuinely industry-leading chief executive, a sporting director of the calibre of Edwin van der Sar who, unlike Jason Wilcox, has the experience, pedigree and knowledge he accumulated as CEO at Ajax. They need a boardroom presence and link to the fans like Bryan Robson.'.

Ratcliffe does not even sit on the United board himself, leaving it to Nevin and John Reece, one of the Ineos co-founders.

It has been revealed that another of his Ineos appointees was the 63-year-old Frenchman Jean-Claude Blanc, an experienced statesman and marketeer with an Olympic, Tour de France and PSG background, who is described as pleasant and without ego – though he was supposedly in the room when the 'scorched' earth comment was made to Ainslie. Blanc was recruited for his gravitas, rather than to pull up trees. He has stepped down from United's board.

Ainslie and Ratcliffe are no longer thought to be friends. Shortly before the alleged episode in the locked aerodrome building, Ainslie observed, in relation to Ratcliffe, that there was a difference between business and sport, where teams were delicately balanced, nuanced groups of people.

‘You want to save money and be efficient, but you’ve got to make sure you look after people. You need that balance,’ he stated. Under the terms of the court settlement, Ainslie gets to keep the boat and sail off into the sunset, leaving Ratcliffe to whatever storms come next.

Speaking at Monday’s press conference ahead of Arsenal’s UEFA Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has given credit to the parents of Jobe Bellingham.

“I think you have to congratulate mum and dad for what they have done because it is incredible. When you look at the two of them [Jobe and Jude Bellingham], they are two amazing footballers – what they are doing is remarkable. Let’s give credit to the parents,” Arteta told reporters ahead of Tuesday’s game at The Emirates.

Jude spent three years in Dortmund from 2020 to 2023 before moving to Real Madrid, where he’s established himself as an notable player. Jobe followed his brother’s footsteps by following him to the Signal Iduna Park when he joined from Sunderland in the summer of 2025.

Although struggling to initially find his feet in 2025/26, Jobe has been on an excellent run of form of late, which has in turn seen him called up to the England national team by Thomas Tuchel during the most recent international break.

With both Bellingham brothers on top of their game at the moment, it is understandable that Arteta chose to praise the parents who have been key to the success of both players.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta stated that Ethan Nwaneri, who is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund from the Gunners, needs to earn the right to play.

“He had started playing quite a lot, and now recently he hasn’t played that much,” the Spaniard said at Monday’s press conference ahead of their UEFA Champions League clash on Tuesday. “He needs to earn the right to play because he is playing at the top of the Bundesliga and the players that they have, they have huge talent and quality. That is the reality of football: you go there, and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn’t give you any advantage so you need to earn it.”.

Nwaneri has only played six minutes of football in Dortmund’s last three games, and has only registered one assist – which came on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim – since his arrival from Arsenal.

Arteta, though, believes the 19-year-old is capable of turning around his current situation. “Ethan first of all has the mindset to do it and then the quality to do it. These things are part of a journey and part of a season, and earn the right to win.”.

Nwaneri could potentially face Arsenal on Tuesday at the Emirates as there is no restriction in his loan deal that prevents him from playing against his parent club. Whether Niko Kovač opts to use him in the game remains to be seen.

#153110. Aberdeen's upcoming manager is a proven overachiever with a big personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1346 w)

Aberdeen's upcoming manager is a proven overachiever with a big personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1346 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event. While unquestionably a successful manager with Motherwell and St Mirren, there was always a lingering doubt about whether his skill set would work at a bigger club with different expectations in terms of style of play. And so it proved.

What didn’t help the Northern Irishman was the perception that those who employed him weren’t exactly bowled over by him in the first place, either.

Robinson would have been a hard enough sell to the Dons support had he been unveiled a few days after Jimmy Thelin departed the scene in January.

That it took them 67 days to deliver confirmation of the appointment – after the club had dalliances with Eirik Horneland and Sandro Schwarz – was hardly a ringing endorsement of their faith in him.

The contrast with the process to appoint Mario Frick is striking. Robinson was sacked two days after a four-goal home thrashing by Hibernian. Five days later, the former Liechtenstein international was named by the Pittodrie club as the new head coach.

After the saga at the start of the year which reflected well on no one, Aberdeen, to give them their dues, knew what they wanted and saw Frick as a hand-in-glove fit. So, what led them so rapidly to his door?

Mario Frick is unveiled at Pittodrie and immediately vowed to transform the club's fortunes.

The 52-year-old, essentially, is a head coach who fits in with the overarching strategy Aberdeen identified several years ago.

This has been lost along the way as poor results have seen a churn of individuals occupy the dug-out, many of whom were square pegs in round holes. This, the club believe, has been why the recruitment has been so random and ineffective.

There’s been little joined-up thinking, as evidenced by the summer window which saw 15 players arrive, many of whom were sub-standard or clearly not part of Robinson’s plan.

The intention always was for the head coach to work in tandem with the sporting director and chief executive rather than independently of them.

While Frick will have a say on what players arrive and depart this January, the conversations around the identity of the team and what’s required to improve it will be three-way.

At Luzern, Frick was happy to trust the judgment of director of football Remo Meyer on such matters.

His willingness to forge the same relationship with Aberdeen’s sporting director, Lutz Pfannenstiel, was the light bulb moment for chief executive Adrian Bevington and chairman Dave Cormack.

Frick earned 125 caps for Liechtenstein and scored 16 goals for the European minnows.

It has been revealed that in keeping with the much-vaunted ‘continental’ model, Pfannenstiel and head of recruitment Darren Mowbray will largely identify players to fit the system. Frick will then be tasked with making it all work.

The strategy is for the squad to be closely aligned with the head coach’s needs rather than assembling the rag bag of players who’ve come in the three windows since Thelin won the Scottish Cup.

There’s much beyond Frick’s willingness to defer matters of player identification to others which caught the eye of the board, however.

Although very much a modern and forward-thinking coach, he’s vastly experienced in the game.

As a player, he turned out for Swiss clubs including St Gallen, Basel, Zurich and Grasshopper.

He became the first Liechtensteiner to play professionally in Italy with AC Arezzo before signing for Verona, Ternana and Siena.

Across 125 internationals, he became Liechtenstein’s all-time top scorer with 16 goals, including one against Scotland at Hampden in 2010, the infamous game which saw Stephen McManus ride to the rescue with a 90th-minute winner.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington welcomes fresh manager Frick to Pittodrie.

Industry observers note that being the star man for an underdog may have had something to do with his upbringing. Frick’s father didn’t exactly encourage him to make it as he started out in the game.

He once revealed in an interview: ‘He told me: ‘There are thousands of talents like you. You won’t make it.’.

His coaching journey began eight years ago with Vaduz, who he succeeded in getting promoted to the Swiss Super League via a play-off.

Sources indicate that appointed head coach of Luzern almost five years ago, he turned the side from relegation candidates into one capable of finishing fourth inside 18 months. There followed finishes of seventh, sixth and seventh place prior to an amicable parting of the ways when his contract expired in May.

Although Frick didn’t win anything, Luzern is not a club which is accustomed to doing so, with their last league title arriving in 1989.

Its supporters still strongly identified with him, though, and recognised that he often got more out of modest resources than he was entitled to.

They enjoyed his major personality – not scared to wind up opponents in the media and not shy at publicly calling out his own players when they didn’t live up to the standards he’d set.

Frick famously scored for Liechtenstein against Scotland in a 2-1 at Hampden in 2010.

When he left there at the end of last season, the supporters felt the loss of a passionate manager who wore his heart on his sleeve, had no time for egos and stopped at nothing to deliver success.

In a recent development, in the Granite City, he will call out anyone not giving their absolute all every moment they are in a red jersey. And unlike the diplomatic Thelin, the fireworks are likely to be seen in public.

If his time at Luzern proves prescient, those who resist or disrupt the dressing room will soon be moved on. Those who do their best by him will have nothing to fear, however.

As Italian football fan Fabio Baccarini will gladly attest, although tough and demanding, Frick is also renowned as being a loyal man with a huge heart.

Baccarini, from Reggio Emilia, became fascinated by Frick in the early 2000s while collecting Panini stickers due to the fact that he played for Liechtenstein, a tiny nation he struggled to pronounce.

He wrote so many letters to his various clubs, hoping to arrange a meeting, that Frick initially feared he might be a stalker.

When they first met in 2011 after a game between Liechtenstein and San Marino, the forward presented Baccarini with a signed shirt, gave him his email address and invited him to a match in Vaduz.

And so began an extraordinary friendship which saw Baccarini regularly drive 1,000km to support the minnows and become their de facto mascot.

Three years back, when Hibs travelled to Luzern in the Conference League, the Italian super-fan was unable to find a bed for the night. Frick ensured he got one in the team hotel at no cost.

The new Pittodrie boss is just the latest to follow in the footsteps of the great Sir Alex Ferguson.

As heartwarming as such tales are, it was, of course, the metrics of on-field success which drew Aberdeen to him.

Frick’s willingness to give young players a chance – another criticism made of Robinson – was a tick against his name.

According to recent reports, he’s handed top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career. He appointed Ardon Jashari, who played against Scotland on Monday, his Luzern captain at the age of 20.

Sources indicate that he does not appear to be wedded to a particular formation. He mostly played a 4-4-2 with a diamond at Luzern, but he’s very much a pragmatist.

When he takes his bow at Rugby Park on Saturday, he’ll select a system to suit the personnel rather than trying to shoehorn the players into a pre-ordained system.

With just two points separating their team from bottom-side Kilmarnock, how the Red Army could do with witnessing a Super Mario bounce.
